'''Jean-Pierre Bourguignon''' (born 21 July 1947) is a French [[mathematician]], working in the field of [[differential geometry]].

==Biography==
Born in [[Lyon]], [[France]], he studied at [[École Polytechnique]] in [[Palaiseau]], graduating in 1969. For his graduate studies he went to [[Paris Diderot University]], where he obtained his [[PhD]] in 1974 under the direction of [[Marcel Berger]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=55339}}</ref>

He was president of the [[Société Mathématique de France]] from 1990 to 1992. From 1995 to 1998, he was president of the [[European Mathematical Society]]. He was director of the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]] near [[Paris]] from 1994 to 2013.  Between 1 January 2014 and 31 December 2019 he was the President of the [[European Research Council]].

{{blockquote|Prof. Bourguignon received the [[Prix Paul Langevin]] in 1987 and the [[Prix du Rayonnement Français]] in Mathematical Sciences and Physics from the [[French Academy of Sciences|Académie des Sciences de Paris]] in 1997. He is a foreign member of the [[Royal Spanish Academy of Sciences]]. In 2005, he was elected honorary member of the [[London Mathematical Society]] and has been the secretary of the mathematics section of the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Bourguignon, Jean-Pierre|title=Abstract for ''When Fundamental Discoveries Meet Daily Life'' (France-HKUST innovation hub inaugural lecture)|publisher=Institute for Advanced Study|website=Digital University Archives, HKUST Library|date=24 March 2017|url=https://archives.ust.hk/dspace/handle/9999/46211}}</ref>}}He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-27 |title=Exceptional scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2026/05/new-fellows-announcement-2026/ |access-date=2026-05-31 |website=Royal Society |language=en}}</ref>
